memory_update.text: Core direct universe for this node should include VRT, ETN, GEV, PWR and CEG as first-pass leaders across cooling/power systems, electrical equipment, grid/power equipment, grid EPC, and nuclear power assets.

POWL is a strong less-obvious electrical-equipment follow-up candidate because management explicitly links medium-voltage switchgear opportunities to larger AI/data-center power demands, but it was left outside the top five due to candidate limit.

Schneider Electric should be tracked via its US ADR SBGSY or non-US primary listing as a global leader in data-center energy management, power distribution, UPS and cooling, but classification as US-listed ADR should be kept distinct from US-domiciled companies.

Need a separate pass for utilities and power asset owners including VST, NEE, SO, DUK, AEP, EXC and AES, because power availability may be regional and regulated-asset-specific rather than a single national market.

Need a separate pass for components/materials and backup/on-site power: HUBB, POWL, CAT, CMI, MTZ, DY, STRL, FLR, ACM, BWXT, LEU, CCJ, SMR, OKLO and battery/storage names may capture narrower chokepoints.

The node should be decomposed into at least five subnodes before scoring: inside-the-fence data-center power/cooling, electrical distribution gear, utility interconnection/grid EPC, generation asset ownership, and fuel/on-site backup power.
POWL should be tracked as a direct medium-voltage switchgear and packaged-power candidate for AI data-center electrical bottlenecks; key risk is project lumpiness and margin extrapolation.
MOD should be tracked as a thermal-infrastructure candidate with explicit >60% expected FY2026 Data Centers revenue growth; verify product mix and liquid-cooling durability.
NVT is a plausible component-level AI data-center power/cooling candidate through intelligent PDUs, enclosures, connectors, and liquid-cooling products, but exact revenue exposure requires evidence.
CAT is a second-order but increasingly direct power-availability candidate via data-center-driven power-generation demand for large engines and turbines.

BE is a direct behind-the-meter power candidate after Oracle's stated intent to procure up to 2.8 GW of fuel-cell systems for AI/cloud infrastructure; contract conversion and financing are key evidence gaps.
Follow-up pass should evaluate HUBB, GEV, ETN, VRT, PWR, CEG, VST, NEE, DUK, SO, ETR, and SMR/OKLO nuclear names separately to avoid crowding this five-candidate limit.
Add POWL as a high-priority electrical-gear candidate for AI data-center power distribution; evidence includes FY2026 backlog growth and a $400M+ data-center order.
Add FIX as a specialty contractor / mechanical-electrical execution candidate; exposure is inferred from technology-sector backlog rather than fully disclosed data-center revenue.
Add ECL as a liquid-cooling candidate contingent on CoolIT transaction closing and integration; this is a non-obvious water/fluid-management mapping to AI thermal infrastructure.
Add CAT as a second-order onsite and backup power-generation beneficiary; data-center applications are explicitly cited in Power Generation sales growth.

Add BE as a high-relevance but higher-risk distributed-power candidate; Oracle 2.8 GW partnership and Equinix deployments support the grid-bypass thesis, but economics and execution need verification.

AI data-center power demand is moving the chokepoint downstream from chips toward electrical distribution, grid interconnection, onsite generation, liquid cooling, and construction/commissioning capacity.

Future Layer 1B passes should test additional second-order candidates in transformers, cables, copper, battery storage, utility interconnection software, turbine supply chains, water utilities, and data-center REIT/customer pass-through economics.

node: Data-center power, cooling, electrical equipment, and grid interconnection
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded universe for the AI data-center power/cooling/grid node. The strongest direct US-listed candidates cluster around: critical data-center power and cooling systems, electrical distribution equipment, grid/power-generation equipment, grid EPC and interconnection services, and contracted baseload generation. This pass prioritizes obvious leaders and directly exposed public assets rather than broad AI semiconductor or software beneficiaries. Expanded the node universe toward US-listed scarce suppliers and infrastructure providers adjacent to AI data-center power constraints. This pass prioritizes direct evidence of exposure to data-center electrical distribution, high-density cooling, grid equipment, behind-the-meter generation, and utility/grid components. No buy/sell view is implied. Expanded the universe around the AI data-center power/cooling/grid chokepoint with five US-listed candidates that are not only obvious hyperscaler/semiconductor names. The strongest direct mappings are Powell Industries for medium-voltage switchgear and packaged electrical systems, Ecolab via its pending CoolIT acquisition for liquid cooling, Caterpillar for power-generation engines/turbines used in data-center applications, Bloom Energy for onsite fuel-cell power when grid interconnection is constrained, and Comfort Systems USA for mechanical/electrical contracting and modular construction capacity serving technology-sector buildouts. This is research mapping only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
